contextBody: Provincial guidance is scoped: BC’s 2023 Physical Security Standards are written for Government of BC facilities, while privacy guidance for BC public libraries focuses on FOIPPA responsibilities. Treat these as planning references, not blanket requirements for private or municipal sites; verify owner, occupancy, applicable code and authority for each project.
sourceTitle: Physical Security Standards for Government of B.C. Facilities; Privacy Guidelines for BC Public Libraries

cctv.note: Source fact: library privacy guidelines address FOIPPA and video surveillance. Question: who controls footage, what purpose/retention/access rules and privacy review apply at this site?
cctv.sourceTitle: Privacy Guidelines for BC Public Libraries

access.note: Source fact: BC publishes government-facility physical-security standards; fire guidance recognizes security/egress conflict. Question: what exit hardware, release sequence and fire-interface review apply?
access.sourceTitle: BC Physical Security Standards; Access, egress and fire door locking or latching device

intrusion.note: Source fact: BC government facility security standards cover physical security planning. Question: identify protected zones, detection coverage, and how intrusion alerts are tested and handed over.
intrusion.sourceTitle: Physical Security Standards for Government of B.C. Facilities

remote.note: Source fact: provincial standards concern government facilities only. Question: who verifies an alert, whom to notify, and what fallback applies during loss of communications? No provincial source establishes a universal monitoring/escalation pathway.
remote.sourceTitle: Physical Security Standards for Government of B.C. Facilities

smart.note: Source fact: BC’s fire/building code page describes minimum code requirements, not building-automation savings. Question: inventory controls, schedules and metering; confirm project code applicability separately.
smart.sourceTitle: BC fire safety codes and bulletins

cyber.note: Source fact: provincial Information Security Policy covers information security, access, physical/environmental security and supply-chain risk for BC government. Question: how are connected cameras/controllers segmented, patched and administered in this owner's environment?

consulting.note: Source fact: the physical-security standards are government-facility-specific and include structured standards. Question: establish site scope, stakeholders, risks, existing systems and decision authority before recommendations.
consulting.sourceTitle: Physical Security Standards for Government of B.C. Facilities

guards.note: Source fact: no general provincial guard requirement established by cited planning materials. Question: what duties, hours, post orders, communications and incident reporting does the owner require? No Fortega availability is implied.
guards.sourceTitle: Physical Security Standards for Government of B.C. Facilities

contextBody: Alberta’s camera guide addresses surveillance in public areas; Alberta Infrastructure’s security guidelines and Green Guide apply to provincial facilities/operations. These sources can structure discovery but do not establish that any particular private or municipal property is subject to those internal guidelines.
sourceTitle: Guide to Using Surveillance Cameras in Public Areas; Physical Security Guidelines & Standards for Government of Alberta Facilities; Efficient Operations of Alberta Infrastructure Facilities

cctv.note: Source fact: Alberta's public-area camera guide discusses collection, policy, design, access/use/disclosure, retention/destruction and audit. Question: determine whether this public-body guidance applies and define purpose, notice, access and retention for the site.
cctv.sourceTitle: Guide to Using Surveillance Cameras in Public Areas

access.note: Source fact: Alberta government facility security guidance discusses access control; provincial fire/building codes supersede it. Question: identify exit function, release sequence and required authority review for actual opening.
access.sourceTitle: Physical Security Guidelines & Standards for Government of Alberta Facilities

intrusion.note: Source fact: Alberta facility guidance includes security design process, access control, base building systems and remote-location facilities. Question: map detection points, alarm ownership, test schedule and escalation contacts.
intrusion.sourceTitle: Physical Security Guidelines & Standards for Government of Alberta Facilities

remote.note: Source fact: facility security guidance includes remote-location considerations, but not universal monitoring obligations. Question: define human verification, contact sequence, response window and comms-loss procedure.
remote.sourceTitle: Physical Security Guidelines & Standards for Government of Alberta Facilities

smart.note: Source fact: Alberta Infrastructure Green Guide promotes energy-efficient operations within its own portfolio and says practices require site adaptation. Question: document existing controls and energy baseline before considering automation changes.
smart.sourceTitle: Efficient Operations of Alberta Infrastructure Facilities

cyber.note: Source fact: Alberta's cybersecurity strategy sets government direction for identifying, managing and responding to cyber threats. Question: assess device accounts, network exposure, updates, vendor access and incident response for the owner's systems.
cyber.sourceTitle: Alberta’s cybersecurity strategy: protecting Alberta’s digital assets

consulting.note: Source fact: Alberta Infrastructure's technical requirements say design guidance is for its facilities and requires professional judgment. Question: confirm owner standards, building type, code review roles and project deliverables.
consulting.sourceTitle: Technical Design Requirements for Alberta Infrastructure Facilities

guards.note: Source fact: Alberta OHS guidance notes isolated security-guard work can pose working-alone hazards and requires employer hazard assessment/control where applicable. Question: assess post-specific hazards, check-in/communication and emergency response; no licensing rule is asserted.
guards.sourceTitle: Occupational health and safety working alone requirements

contextBody: Saskatchewan states that 2020 national building, fire and energy codes took effect January 1, 2024. Government IT security policies have a government/partner scope, and its CCTV policy is correctional-facility-specific. Verify applicable code and owner requirements for each property; do not generalize internal policies.
sourceTitle: National Building Code, National Fire Code, National Energy Code for Buildings; Information Security Policies; CCTV and Remote Monitoring Systems

cctv.note: Source fact: Saskatchewan correctional CCTV policy requires balancing privacy with facility safety/security; scope limited to adult correctional facilities. Question: for a non-correctional site, determine applicable privacy framework, purpose, retention and access controls.
cctv.sourceTitle: 517 - Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) and Remote Monitoring Systems

access.note: Source fact: provincial codes set minimum requirements for building construction and fire-safe operation. Question: verify the applicable code/authority review and ensure any electronic locking proposal preserves compliant egress.
access.sourceTitle: National Building Code, National Fire Code, National Plumbing Code and National Energy Code for Buildings

intrusion.note: Source fact: Saskatchewan IT physical/environmental security policy covers unauthorized physical access to government information/facilities, scoped to government processes and assets. Question: identify zones, detection objectives, testing and incident ownership.

remote.note: Source fact: correctional CCTV/remote monitoring policy defines monitoring in its correctional setting only. Question: define who receives alarms/video, verifies incidents and escalates, and what happens during connectivity failure.
remote.sourceTitle: 517 - Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) and Remote Monitoring Systems

smart.note: Source fact: Saskatchewan describes smart metering, real-time monitoring and audits as energy-efficiency approaches, including public facilities. Question: establish available meters, control points and baseline; no site savings implied.

cyber.note: Source fact: provincial information-security policies align to ISO/IEC 27001 and include risk assessment/treatment for government context. Question: review network separation, credentials, firmware, vendor access and incident plan for connected systems.

consulting.note: Source fact: Saskatchewan code adoption establishes minimum provincial standards and local authorities administer/enforce building construction. Question: scope site-specific code, stakeholder and system-interface review with the appropriate authority.
consulting.sourceTitle: National Building Code, National Fire Code, National Plumbing Code and National Energy Code for Buildings

guards.note: Source fact: cited provincial sources do not establish general guard staffing requirements. Question: clarify site risk, coverage, post instructions, supervision, communications and reporting; no licensing requirement or availability implied.

contextBody: Manitoba sources include social-housing design guidance covering building access, video monitoring, fire/life safety and energy efficiency; it is scoped to multi-unit affordable/social housing. Provincial energy code adoption and general cyber controls provide additional context, not site-specific determinations.
sourceTitle: Design Guidelines for Multi-unit Affordable and Social Housing; Manitoba Energy Code for Buildings; Baseline Cyber Security Controls for Small and Medium Organizations

cctv.note: Source fact: Manitoba Housing design guidance includes video monitoring for its multi-unit affordable/social housing design scope. Question: establish authority, intended purpose, privacy protections, access and retention for this property.
cctv.sourceTitle: Design Guidelines for Multi-unit Affordable and Social Housing

access.note: Source fact: the same design guidance covers building access and fire/life safety in its housing scope. Question: document opening/exit role and release operation; confirm current requirements with the applicable building/fire authority.
access.sourceTitle: Design Guidelines for Multi-unit Affordable and Social Housing

intrusion.note: Source fact: design guidance includes a security chapter, while Manitoba Housing materials describe electronic security systems in its housing context. Question: determine the actual detection objective, alarm routing and test ownership.
intrusion.sourceTitle: Design Guidelines for Multi-unit Affordable and Social Housing

remote.note: Source fact: Manitoba Housing describes a 24-hour communications centre for Winnipeg tenants, not a provincewide commercial monitoring service. Question: identify this owner's actual response contacts and escalation process; do not assume municipal dispatch integration.

smart.note: Source fact: Manitoba Energy Code for Buildings adopts the National Energy Code for Buildings 2020, effective January 1, 2024. Question: confirm applicability and document building controls/energy baseline before evaluating automation opportunities.
smart.sourceTitle: Manitoba Energy Code for Buildings, M.R. 79/2023

cyber.note: Source fact: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security baseline controls published by Manitoba are recommendations for small and medium organizations; it identifies system-owner responsibility for cyber risk. Question: inventory connected devices and assess authentication, patching, backups and incident response.
cyber.sourceTitle: Baseline Cyber Security Controls for Small and Medium Organizations v1.2

consulting.note: Source fact: Manitoba Housing design guidelines describe an integrated design process and design submissions for their defined housing projects. Question: align discovery, system interfaces, authority reviews and commissioning with this project's actual scope.
consulting.sourceTitle: Design Guidelines for Multi-unit Affordable and Social Housing

guards.note: Source fact: cited sources do not establish a general guard staffing obligation. Question: clarify whether staffing is desired, site coverage, duties, supervision, communications and incident documentation; no licensing or Fortega availability implied.
